newsitem.title: FINLAND: M-SERLA SAYS MARKETS TO HELP FROM NOW ON.
newsitem.headline: M-SERLA SAYS MARKETS TO HELP FROM NOW ON.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla said on Thursday that markets had not helped group earnings yet this year but would do so from now.
"So far, markets have not helped us, from now on markets will help us," CEO Jorma Vaajoki told a news conference referring to pulp, fine paper and printing paper markets.
The group earlier reported first-half earnings after financial items rose 37 percent to 306 million markka from 223 million in the year-ago period.
Vaajoki said this year's fall in prices had been so strong that foreign exchange developments -- the dollar and sterling have been surging -- had not fully offset the decline.
Metsa-Serla said it expected magazine paper prices and profitability in the segment to improve.
"Magazine paper prices and profitability are expected to improve in the second half of the year," it said in its interim report.
Metsa-Serla also said it expected an increase pulp prices to boost fine paper prices which would on balance help the profitability of fine paper products.
"If they materialise, pulp price hikes will give an impulse to the fine paper industry to lift prices," it said.
"Despite the higher cost effect of pulp price rises, fine paper mills' profitability should rise in the second half compared to the first."
